stories.headline: Google just shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash and a cybersecurity-specific variant
stories.blurb: DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 Flash, a new lightweight model, alongside 3.8 Flash Cyber—a version trained specifically for security tasks. Flash Cyber is designed to handle threat detection, vulnerability analysis, and security code review faster than general models.
stories.why_it_matters: Security teams can now use a model built for their workflow instead of prompt-engineering a general LLM
stories.original_headline: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber

stories.headline: Anthropic cuts Claude's agentic coding costs by up to 45 percent
stories.blurb: Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models cost 25 percent less for typical tasks and up to 45 percent less for complex agent work compared to the previous generation. The update also loosens safeguards and adjusts data retention policies based on customer feedback.
stories.why_it_matters: Running AI agents in production just got cheaper, which makes longer autonomous workflows financially viable.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work

stories.headline: Cursor can now run on your own servers
stories.blurb: Cursor now supports self-hosted machines, meaning you can keep all code execution and tooling inside your own network instead of Cursor's cloud. This matters for teams with strict data residency rules or proprietary codebases that can't leave internal infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: You can finally use Cursor's AI coding tools without sending code to external servers.

stories.headline: Uber just launched self-driving cars in London with British AI startup Wayve
stories.blurb: Uber and Wayve are running robotaxis on London's narrow, winding streets — a harder test than LA or San Francisco. Wayve's AI learned to drive by training on UK roads instead of being programmed with endless rules, making it easier to deploy in new cities with different layouts.
stories.why_it_matters: Self-driving cars are finally leaving American grid cities for Europe's medieval street networks.
stories.original_headline: Uber, Wayve Launch Robotaxi Service in London to Compete With Waymo
